title: Late-scale signal correction and burst safety for dedicated pools
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Multiple Dedicated customers reported intermittent 5-15s tail latency spikes and failed request admission during traffic bursts. Root cause triage indicates the autoscaler was not starting new reserved workers quickly enough because the scale signal (latency-derived) was suppressed by a long smoothing window and the pool reservation token accounting had a race that allowed tokens to be reclaimed prematurely. This ticket tracks the bugfix, short-term mitigations, test plan, and post-release verification for runtime-1.19.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Ava Martinez: Initial incident reported by AcmeHealth SREs; page ops team observed queue growth and rejected requests when bursts exceeded burst_limit. Created hotfix branch and escalation thread.

2025-02-13 - Rishi Kapoor: Reproduced locally with synthetic burst runner. Observed autoscaler "no-op" when 95th-latency climbed quickly; smoothing window of 60s delayed scale actions. Also observed ReservationEvictor reclaiming tokens after transient worker heartbeats delay.
2025-02-14 - Priya Singh (SRE): Deployed temporary policy: lower smoothing window to 15s and increase burst headroom to 20% for affected tenants. This reduced incidents but not a long-term fix.

2025-02-15 - Engineering leads review: Agreed on two-pronged approach: 1) fix late-scale detection by switching to an exponential moving average with adaptive half-life, 2) harden reservation accounting to avoid double-free/race conditions and add sanity checks preventing eviction during ongoing scale-ups.
2025-02-16 - Rishi Kapoor: Drafted RFC and implementation plan. PR #4821 created (see attachments). Will run canary in us-west-2 with two high-throughput tenants.
2025-02-18 - QA: Added stress test scripts and automated validation to the CI pipeline to assert no regression in scale-down behavior under steady load.
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler detects burst signals and launches additional reserved workers within target SLO of 30s in our synthetic burst test harness
Reservation token race condition eliminated: no double-free observed in 10k synthetic scale events run
Canary rollout completed in us-west-2 for two tenants for 48h with no request rejects attributable to pool depletion
New telemetry added: scale_decision_latency_ms, reservation_evictions_per_min, predicted_headroom_pct visible in Console
Automated regression tests added to CI and to chaos stress suite
rollout_notes: Step 1: Merge PR and build runtime-1.19-canary image tagged 'autoscale-fix-42890'
Step 2: Deploy canary to us-west-2 reserved cluster (non-production tenants + two pilot customers who agreed)
Step 3: Monitor metrics for 48h, run synthetic burst injection every 6h, and validate no rejects and acceptable latency
Step 4: Gradual deployment to remaining Dedicated clusters over 72h if canary stable; rollback window 2h after each stage
Step 5: Notify Customer Success and affected tenants with rollout plan and expected improvements
root_cause_summary: Two contributing issues: 1) The latency-based scale signal used a static 60s smoothing window which caused delayed reactions to sudden bursts. 2) A race in the reservation token lifecycle allowed ReservationEvictor to reclaim tokens when workers were in transient 'heartbeating' state, which reduced effective pool capacity during scale-up.
mitigation_and_fix: Code changes: replace fixed smoothing with EMA with adaptive half-life (shorter for sudden rises), add a minimum scale_guard_time to avoid oscillation, and add a reservation state machine to prevent token reclamation until worker registration/heartbeat completes. Operational mitigations: temporarily reduce smoothing to 15s and raise burst headroom by 20% for critical customers. Telemetry: emit new metrics and alerts for 'scale_decision_delay' and 'unexpected_eviction'.
follow_up_tasks: Post-deploy: run a 7-day regression window and produce metrics report comparing pre/post 95th and 99th latency
Add documented runbook for Autonomous Burst Response that ties autoscaler decisions to fallback routing policies
Audit all eviction timers across Dedicated to ensure consistent semantics
Product: review burst quota UI to surface headroom and predicted need to customers
SRE: schedule a failure-injection exercise testing eviction during scale-up
